6127.stem:
Jennifer is an environmental scientist who needs to measure the depth of a lake. She drops a rope with a weight on one end and lets it sink to the bottom, labelled $A$. Ensuring the rope is tight, she records the length of rope as 16.2 m, as shown in the diagram below. The angle of depression from the boat to the anchor is $49^\circ$.

\exfigure{497_q35_1}

figures.cap: boat on lake with rope of 16.2 m to anchor A, angle of depression 49 degrees

parts.latex: What is the depth of the lake, to the nearest tenth of a metre?

Due to the difficulty of keeping the rope taught and the movement of the boat in the water, Jennifer estimates that the measurement of the angle has an error of $2^\circ$ and the length of the rope has an error of 0.1 m.

What is the upper and lower bound for the depth of the lake?

solutions.latex:
The angle between the rope and the vertical is $90 - 49 = 41^\circ$.

In the right-angled triangle, the depth $x$ is adjacent to this angle:
$$\cos 41^\circ = \dfrac{x}{16.2}$$
$$\begin{aligned} x &= 16.2\cos 41^\circ \\ &\approx 12.2 \text{ m} \end{aligned}$$
criteria: Finds the angle $41^\circ$ or sets up the ratio, or equivalent merit

solutions.latex:
The depth is $x = L\cos\theta$, which is smallest for the largest angle and shortest rope.

Smallest: angle $41 + 2 = 43^\circ$, rope $16.2 - 0.1 = 16.1$ m.
$$\begin{aligned} x &= 16.1 \cos 43^\circ \\ &\approx 11.8 \end{aligned}$$
Largest: angle $41 - 2 = 39^\circ$, rope $16.2 + 0.1 = 16.3$ m.
$$\begin{aligned} x &= 16.3 \cos 39^\circ \\ &\approx 12.7 \end{aligned}$$
$$\therefore\ \text{lower bound } 11.8 \text{ m, upper bound } 12.7 \text{ m}$$
criteria: Finds one bound, or equivalent merit

497_q35_1.notes: Boat as a half-ellipse on wavy water, plus the horizontal segment at the stern and the 49° arc with its leader. The rope and lake bed are house aux dashes (the scan's rope dashes are heavy; rule 3 forbids that). The vertical depth line is fine dotted. A is a dot, and the rope label has its leader. NOT TO SCALE is kept. The scan's stray mark at top right is left out. Most of the remaining colour is the water's wave phase, the heavy scanned rope stroke, and labels a few px off (the round-1 compile failure used up a round). Rules 1, 3, 4, 11, 17.

$$\sin 71^\circ 40' = \dfrac{BD}{880}$$

$$\begin{aligned} BD &= 880 \times \sin 71^\circ 40' \\ &\approx 835 \\ &\approx 840 \text{ m} \end{aligned}$$

figures.cap: triangle TPS with angles 73 and 49 degrees and PS = 48 m

parts.latex:
The points $T$, $P$ and $S$ are on a level block of land.

\exfigure{496_q18_1}

Calculate the distance from the base of the tree, $T$, to the point $S$.

Answer correct to two decimal places.

solutions.latex:
Angles in triangle $PTS$ sum to $180^\circ$:
$$\begin{aligned} \angle PTS &= 180^\circ - 73^\circ - 49^\circ \\ &= 58^\circ \end{aligned}$$
Using the sine rule, with $x = TS$ opposite the $49^\circ$ angle:
$$\dfrac{x}{\sin 49^\circ} = \dfrac{48}{\sin 58^\circ}$$
$$\begin{aligned} x &= \dfrac{48\sin 49^\circ}{\sin 58^\circ} \\ &\approx 42.72 \text{ m} \end{aligned}$$
criteria: Finds $\angle PTS$ or sets up the sine rule, or equivalent merit

meta.format_note: Rubric written by us (source had none).

496_q18_1.notes: Triangle TPS kept at the crop's shape, which is NOT TO SCALE. The slight slope of TP is kept because it is part of the drawing, not scan tilt. The tree at T is redrawn as a simple grey canopy with a trunk. Labels S, T, P, 73°, 49°, '48 m' and 'Not to scale' are at the crop's positions and size (fixed in round 2). Rules used: 1, 2, 3, 11, 19.

parts.latex: A magpie is 8 metres above ground level in a tree. The magpie sees an earthworm on the ground at an angle of depression of $35^\circ$. How far must the magpie fly in a straight line to catch the earthworm, assuming the earthworm does not move?

solutions.latex:
The angle of depression equals the angle of elevation from the earthworm, $35^\circ$. In the right-angled triangle, the height $8$ m is opposite this angle and the flight path $x$ is the hypotenuse.

$$\sin 35^\circ = \dfrac{8}{x}$$

$$\begin{aligned} x &= \dfrac{8}{\sin 35^\circ} \\ &\approx 13.9 \text{ m} \end{aligned}$$

Hence the answer is option D.

figures.cap: right triangle with legs 20 and 16, hypotenuse x, angle theta

parts.latex: Find the value of $\theta$, correct to the nearest degree.
Find the value of $x$, correct to one decimal place.

solutions.latex:
The sides $16$ and $20$ are the opposite and adjacent sides to $\theta$, so use tangent.

$$\tan\theta = \dfrac{16}{20}$$

$$\begin{aligned} \theta &= \tan^{-1}\dfrac{16}{20} \\ &\approx 39^\circ \text{ (nearest degree)} \end{aligned}$$

meta.format_note: Rubric written by us (source had none).

solutions.latex:
Using Pythagoras' theorem in the right-angled triangle:

$$\begin{aligned} x^2 &= 20^2 + 16^2 \\ &= 656 \end{aligned}$$

$$\begin{aligned} x &= \sqrt{656} \\ &\approx 25.6 \text{ (1 d.p.)} \end{aligned}$$

meta.format_note: Rubric written by us (source had none). Source alternative gives 25.4 from the rounded angle; the main answer is 25.6.
meta.corrected: Corrected from source: a second answer $25.4$ (from the rounded angle) was given beside $25.6$.
meta.overwritten_from_source: Corrected from source: a second answer $25.4$ (from the rounded angle) was given beside $25.6$.

6325.stem:
A 15 m platform ($AB$) extends from the top of one side of a building as shown in the diagram below. Point $C$, at ground level, is measured to be at angles of depression of $42^\circ$ and $60^\circ$ from points $A$ and $B$ respectively.

\exfigure{716_q18_1}

figures.cap: building with platform AB, points C and D at ground level
solution sketch: diagram with angles of depression marked and lines CA, CB drawn

parts.latex: Explain why $\angle BCA = 18^\circ$.
Using the sine rule, show that the distance from $A$ to $C$ is $42.04$ metres.
What is the height of the building, correct to the nearest metre?

solutions.latex:
\exfigure{716_q18_s1}

$\angle ABC$ is obtuse and lies on a straight line with the $60^\circ$ angle of depression at $B$.
$$\angle ABC = 180^\circ - 60^\circ = 120^\circ \text{ (straight line)}$$
Using the angle sum of triangle $ABC$:
$$\begin{aligned} \angle BCA &= 180^\circ - 42^\circ - 120^\circ \\ &= 18^\circ \end{aligned}$$

Let $AC = x$. By the sine rule in triangle $ABC$:
$$\dfrac{x}{\sin 120^\circ} = \dfrac{15}{\sin 18^\circ}$$
$$\begin{aligned} x &= \dfrac{15\sin 120^\circ}{\sin 18^\circ} \\ &= 42.0375\ldots \\ &\approx 42.04 \text{ m} \end{aligned}$$
as required.
criteria: Writes the sine rule with correct substitution, or equivalent merit

solutions.latex:
Let $h$ be the height of the building. In the right-angled triangle, the angle at $A$ between $AC$ and the vertical is $90^\circ - 42^\circ = 48^\circ$.
$$\cos 48^\circ = \dfrac{h}{42.04}$$
$$\begin{aligned} h &= 42.04\cos 48^\circ \\ &= 28.13\ldots \\ &\approx 28 \text{ m} \end{aligned}$$
criteria: Writes a correct trigonometric equation for $h$, or equivalent merit

meta.format_note: Rubric written by us. Added the source-implied reason for the $48^\circ$ angle.

716_q18_1.notes: Platform AB (light blue in the crop, drawn in grey per rule 6), brick wall at A–D, ground CD, the four points, 15 m label and the 'Not to scale' note, all at the crop's positions. The brick wall has the crop's 20 courses with joints on every second course. The scores are below 0.85 only because the scan's brick lines don't line up with mine to the pixel. Rules 1, 2, 3, 6.

716_q18_s1.notes: Same building as the question figure, plus the solution's lines CA and CB, a fine dashed horizontal through B, and true arcs for the 60° depression at B and the 42° depression at A. The figure is not to scale, so the arcs follow the drawn lines and the geometry was not changed. The '15 m' label is moved above the platform so the 42° value has clear space (rules 11, 22). The teacher's hand marks are cleaned up (rule 17). The low scores come from the handwritten ink in the crop.

figures.cap: Leaning Tower of Pisa with right triangle, 5.6 m, 54.5 m, angle theta

solutions.latex:
In the right-angled triangle in the diagram, the side of length $5.6$ m is opposite $\theta$, and the hypotenuse is $54.5$ m.

Opposite and hypotenuse are related by the sine ratio, $\sin\theta=\dfrac{\text{opposite}}{\text{hypotenuse}}$.
$$\sin\theta=\dfrac{5.6}{54.5}$$
Hence
$$\theta=\sin^{-1}\left(\dfrac{5.6}{54.5}\right)$$
Options C and D use tangent, which would need the adjacent side. Option B has the ratio upside down, which is greater than 1.

meta.generated_note: MCQ working written for key A.

1247_q10_1.notes: Detailed illustration of the Leaning Tower of Pisa next to the right-triangle sketch. The artwork cannot be redrawn in TikZ, so the crop is kept.

6457.stem:
The diagram below shows a triangle $ABC$ where $AB=20$ cm and $\angle ACB=52^\circ$. Point $D$ lies on $BC$ such that $AD$ is perpendicular to $BC$. The length of $BD$ is 18 cm.

\exfigure{850_q17_1}

parts.latex: Find the length of $AD$, correct to two decimal places.
Hence, find the length of $CD$, correct to the nearest centimetre.

solutions.latex:
In right-angled triangle $ABD$, by Pythagoras' theorem:
$$\begin{aligned}AD&=\sqrt{20^2-18^2}\\&=8.717797\ldots\\&\approx 8.72 \text{ cm (to 2 d.p.)}\end{aligned}$$
criteria: Applies Pythagoras' theorem, or equivalent merit

solutions.latex:
In right-angled triangle $ACD$, use the tangent ratio.
$$\begin{aligned}\tan 52^\circ&=\dfrac{AD}{CD}\\CD&=\dfrac{AD}{\tan 52^\circ}\\&=\dfrac{8.717797\ldots}{\tan 52^\circ}\\&=6.811\ldots\end{aligned}$$
$$\therefore CD=7 \text{ cm (to the nearest centimetre)}$$
criteria: Applies a trigonometric ratio, or equivalent merit

850_q17_1.notes: Triangle ABC with altitude AD, right-angle box at D, 52° arc at C ending on both arms (round 2 fixed the arc direction). Labels as crop, clear of lines (rules 1, 11, 22).

figures.cap: triangle PQR with PQ = 12 m, angle P = 53 degrees, angle R = 18 degrees

parts.latex:
What is the distance from $Q$ to $R$ in the diagram below, correct to the nearest metre?

\exfigure{819_q6_1}

solutions.latex:
In $\triangle PQR$, $PQ = 12$ m is opposite $\angle R = 18^\circ$, and $QR$ is opposite $\angle P = 53^\circ$.

Applying the sine rule,
$$\dfrac{QR}{\sin 53^\circ} = \dfrac{12}{\sin 18^\circ}$$
$$\begin{aligned} QR &= \dfrac{12\sin 53^\circ}{\sin 18^\circ} \\ &\approx 31.0 \text{ m} \end{aligned}$$
So $QR \approx 31$ m, which is option B.

The crop marks no angle arcs, so none are drawn. NOT TO SCALE sits about 15 px lower than in the crop and 53° a few px to the right. Both are clear of every line (rule 11). Lines are 0.6pt although the scan's are heavier (rule 3).

figures.cap: right triangle with angle 28 degrees and vertical side 700 m, not to scale

parts.latex:
An aeroplane climbs at an angle of $28^\circ$ to the horizontal. Find to the nearest metre the distance travelled along its flight path while rising 700m vertically. Express your answer to the nearest metre.

\exfigure{821_q19_1}

solutions.latex:
The flight path is the hypotenuse and $700$ m is opposite the $28^\circ$ angle, so use sine.
$$\sin 28^\circ=\dfrac{700}{x}$$
$$\begin{aligned} x &= \dfrac{700}{\sin 28^\circ} \\ &= 1491.038\ldots \\ &\approx 1491 \text{ m} \end{aligned}$$
criteria: Sets up a correct trigonometric equation, or equivalent merit

It has the angle arc with 28°, a right-angle box, 700 m and NOT TO SCALE. The decorative aeroplane clip-art is left out, and the green lines are drawn black (rule 6). The original score of 0.73 is almost all the aeroplane picture and the thicker green strokes. Rules used: 1, 3, 6, 11, 14.

figures.cap: right-angled triangle, hypotenuse 150, angle 20 degrees, side x

solutions.latex:
The side $x$ is opposite the $20^\circ$ angle and 150 is the hypotenuse, so use sine.
$$\begin{aligned} \sin 20^\circ &= \dfrac{x}{150} \\ x &= 150\sin 20^\circ \end{aligned}$$
So the answer is D.

figures.cap: swimming pool cross-section, 25 m long, 1.3 m shallow end, 2°17' incline, depth d m

parts.latex:
The floor of a swimming pool inclines at $2^\circ 17'$ to the horizontal. The shallow end is 1.3 m deep and the pool is 25 m long. What is the depth $d$ m, to the nearest 0.1 m, at the deep end?

\exfigure{826_q24_1}

solutions.latex:
The pool floor, the horizontal and the vertical rise form a right-angled triangle with angle $2^\circ 17'$, opposite side $h$ and adjacent side $25$ m.
$$\tan 2^\circ 17' = \dfrac{h}{25}$$
$$\begin{aligned} h &= 25 \times \tan 2^\circ 17' \\ &= 0.996819\ldots \end{aligned}$$
$$\begin{aligned} d &= 1.3 + 0.996819\ldots \\ &\approx 2.3 \text{ m} \end{aligned}$$
The depth at the deep end is $2.3$ m.
criteria: Uses the correct trigonometric ratio, or equivalent merit

826_q24_1.notes: Pool cross-section as in the crop: brown ground → flat grey shade, blue water → lighter grey with a smooth wavy surface, floor from (shallow, 1.3 m) to the deep corner, dashed aux horizontal meeting the floor's start, right-angle mark, angle arc at the shallow corner with the label 2°17′ (halo on the shading). The 1.3 m and d m dimension arrows with extension lines, 25 m, and the diving board, post and rope in outline (yellow removed). The original score is low only because the crop's solid brown ground fill is counted as ink; all lines and labels coincide. Round 2 fixed the arc direction and the water fill. Rules 1,4,5,5b,6,12.

solutions.latex:
In the right-angled triangle, $BC$ is adjacent to $\angle ABC$ and $AB$ is the hypotenuse, so use cosine.

$$\begin{aligned} \cos\angle ABC &= \dfrac{12}{16} \\ \angle ABC &= \cos^{-1}\left(\dfrac{12}{16}\right) \\ &= 41^\circ24'35'' \\ &\approx 41^\circ25' \end{aligned}$$

Hence the correct option is the one giving $41^\circ25'$.

827_q11_1.notes: Right triangle ACB with the right-angle box at C. The 16 cm label is rotated along the hypotenuse and 12 cm is centred under BC. Proportions follow the crop, not the true 16/12 ratio (rule 1). The scan's heavy strokes are drawn at 0.6pt (rule 3).

figures.cap: ramp PQ at 37 degrees with points S, T, W, R

parts.latex: Use Trigonometry to calculate the distance $QT$ correct to TWO decimal places.
What is the horizontal distance $TW$ in the diagram, correct to 1 decimal place?

solutions.latex:
In right-angled triangle $QST$ (hypotenuse $QS=1.6$ m), the cosine ratio gives
$$\cos 37^\circ=\dfrac{QT}{1.6}$$
$$\begin{aligned} QT &= 1.6\cos 37^\circ \\ &\approx 1.28 \text{ m} \end{aligned}$$
$$\therefore\ QT \approx 1.28 \text{ m}$$

Similar triangles have corresponding sides in proportion:
$$\dfrac{2}{1.6}=\dfrac{QW}{1.28}$$
$$QW=1.6$$
$$\begin{aligned} TW &= 1.6-1.28 \\ &= 0.32 \\ &\approx 0.3 \text{ m} \end{aligned}$$
$$\therefore\ TW \approx 0.3 \text{ m}$$
criteria: Uses similar triangles to find $QW$, or equivalent merit

827_q35_1.notes: Ramp QP and bench QR, kept at the crop's angle (about 27°) although it is labelled 37°, because the figure is NOT TO SCALE (rule 1). Also drawn: the black coin rectangle on the ramp, dashed perpendiculars from S and P with right-angle marks, the 40 cm and 1.6 m dimension arrows parallel to the ramp, and a dashed T–W arrow ending clear of the T and W labels (rule 11). The 37° arc ends on the ramp and has a filled head. Ramp and bench are 0.6pt where the crop is heavy (rule 3); most remaining red is that stroke weight. The NOT TO SCALE text is slightly smaller to match the crop's width.
